items.stem: At steady state in a completely mixed reactor operating with no reaction, the mass rate of a conservative substance leaving the reactor equals:

options.text: The mass rate entering the reactor
options.rationale: Correct: at steady state with no reaction or accumulation, mass in equals mass out.

options.text: Zero, because the reactor stores all mass
options.rationale: At steady state there is no accumulation, so storage is not increasing.
Nothing in a conservative steady-state balance doubles the throughput.

options.text: The reactor volume times the flow rate
options.rationale: That product has the wrong units and is not a mass rate.

items.explanation: Correct: at steady state with no reaction or accumulation, mass in equals mass out.

items.stem: Two future cash flows are compared using present worth at interest rate i. Doubling i will generally:

options.text: Reduce the present worth of future cash flows
options.rationale: Correct: a higher discount rate lowers the present worth of future amounts.

options.text: Increase the present worth of future cash flows
options.rationale: Higher discounting decreases, not increases, present worth.
Present worth is sensitive to the interest rate.

options.text: Only affect the first year's cash flow
options.rationale: All future cash flows are discounted more heavily, not just the first.

items.explanation: Correct: a higher discount rate lowers the present worth of future amounts.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about a hazard quotient (HQ) used in risk screening are correct?

options.text: It is computed as exposure divided by a reference dose (or concentration)
An HQ greater than 1 indicates a potential for non-cancer concern
options.rationale: Correct: HQ > 1 flags that exposure exceeds the reference value.

options.text: An HQ directly gives the probability of developing cancer
options.rationale: HQ addresses non-cancer screening, not cancer probability.

options.text: HQ is independent of the magnitude of exposure
options.rationale: HQ scales directly with exposure, so it is not independent of it.

options.text: HQ can be computed without any toxicity reference value
options.rationale: A reference dose or concentration is required to compute HQ.

items.explanation: Correct keys: A, B. Correct: HQ = exposure / reference value. Correct: HQ > 1 flags that exposure exceeds the reference value.
